reason: Several named characters in this passage are not leaders. Asenath (אָֽסְנַ֗ת), Joseph's wife and daughter of Potipherah, priest of On, is explicitly named but has no leadership role—she is presented only as Joseph's wife and mother to his children. Additionally, Manasseh (מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה) and Ephraim (אֶפְרָ֑יִם), Joseph's two sons, are named but are infants without any leadership position or authority. While Pharaoh, Joseph (who becomes vizier), Potipherah (priest), and the chief officials are indeed leaders, the existence of named non-leaders (particularly Asenath and the two sons) falsifies the claim that only leaders are named.
